title: Provider slot activation reducer
description: Objective: close the missing production RESERVED→ACTIVE provider-slot transition required by the daemon effect.activate path. Deliverable: extend the public @moe/scheduler ProviderSlotReservation closure with an immutable slot dimension and nullable attempt binding, make reserveProviderSlot return a dimension-bound RESERVED record, and expose activateProviderSlot that exact-parses the record/command, verifies slot/request identity, accepts only RESERVED, and returns ACTIVE bound to the exact attempt without mutating its inputs. Consumer: task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d must import and call this public root surface after @moe/runner activateEffect succeeds. NOT in scope: daemon ingress or persistence, effect/budget transitions, provider launch, release/terminal cleanup, or recovery policy. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && a plain-Node @moe/scheduler root export/transition smoke.
definitionOfDone: reserveProviderSlot exact-validates dimension/slot/request inputs and returns a deeply frozen `{dimension, slotRef, requestId, state:"RESERVED", attemptRef:null}` successor without mutating caller data.
Public activateProviderSlot accepts only an exact RESERVED predecessor plus exact expected slot/request identity and nonempty attemptRef, returning a frozen ACTIVE successor bound to that attempt.

Malformed input returns AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT and wrong-state, replayed, or identity-mismatched activation returns AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE; focused tests pin each exact production code and prove no ACTIVE successor is present.
@moe/scheduler root exports activateProviderSlot and the complete command/result type closure; a plain-Node package-root smoke exercises RESERVED→ACTIVE.
The focused scheduler typecheck/tests pass, and a mutation of the production RESERVED-state guard makes the named replay/wrong-state test fail.

Model + reducer landed; the whole lease-resource.test.ts file is now GREEN (27/27), and the only remaining scheduler red is index-surface.test.ts's 3-arg root call, which is step 4's work.

resource-model.ts:
- ProviderSlotReservation gained `readonly dimension: string` and `readonly attemptRef: string | null`.
- New exported ProviderSlotActivateCommand `{dimension, slotRef, requestId, attemptRef}` — attemptRef non-nullable there, since a command that binds nothing is not an activation.
- New exact parsers parseProviderSlot / parseProviderSlotActivation. Both go through `exactRecord` (isPlainRecord + hasOnlyOwnStringKeys + readOwnDataProperty), then destructure to locals and REBUILD a fresh record. No cast of an unparsed caller object and no spread of one, so an accessor/proxy/extra key cannot survive the parse and reappear in a successor.
- `attemptRef !== null && !isRef(attemptRef)` is deliberate: only literal null means unbound; every other non-ref stays malformed rather than degrading to "absent" (a malformed-as-absent read would let a junk attempt authorize the weaker unbound branch).

lease-resource.ts:
- reserveProviderSlot is now `(value, dimension, slotRef, requestId)` — dimension as the 4th fact / 2nd positional, matching the plan's step-6 smoke literal — and returns `{dimension, slotRef, requestId, state:'RESERVED', attemptRef:null}` frozen. No default dimension anywhere: the daemon counts slot ceilings per dimension, so a reducer-side default would silently merge two ceilings.
- activateProviderSlot(predecessor, command): parses BOTH first and returns AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT if either is malformed, then refuses AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE on the first semantic mismatch in fixed order — dimension/slotRef identity, requestId identity, `state !== 'RESERVED'`, `attemptRef !== null` — otherwise returns a rebuilt frozen ACTIVE record bound to the command's attemptRef.
- Nothing is mutated, frozen, or returned by reference from either input; the successor is constructed field-by-field from the parsed values, not spread from the predecessor.
- No release/persistence/terminal behavior added, per the NOT-in-scope list.
